about.title: Mission Viejo Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Mission Viejo's roads carry residents between neighborhoods, schools, and the I-5 every day, and most trips end without incident. In 2025, though, the city recorded 210 injury collisions, with 289 people injured and 3 traffic deaths. Public records show the highest counts along the San Diego Freeway, Marguerite Parkway, Alicia Parkway, and Los Alisos Boulevard, and reported crashes tend to cluster on Tuesday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. Those are simply the numbers; they say nothing about who was at fault in your case. What matters after a crash is what you do next. Photograph the scene if you can, get the names of witnesses, and see a doctor even if you feel mostly fine. Then be careful with the other driver's insurer. Their adjuster may ask for a recorded statement, and you are not required to give one. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Mission Viejo residents with an independent personal injury attorney who works on contingency, so there is no fee unless your case recovers money.

whyChoose.title: Why Mission Viejo Drivers Use LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines are shorter than people expect
items.desc: California generally gives you two years to file a car accident lawsuit, but a claim against a city, county, or state agency can require notice in as little as six months. An early connection with an attorney keeps those dates from slipping past.

items.title: Partial fault does not end your claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you share some blame, with your compensation reduced by your percentage. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to assign you more fault than the evidence supports.

items.title: Free to connect, contingency to hire
items.desc: LawProactive costs nothing, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency. That means no attorney fee unless your case results in a recovery, and California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in ordinary car accident cases.

items.question: I was rear-ended on Alicia Parkway and the other insurer wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not obligated to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company, and it is usually wise to hold off. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to minimize your injuries or shift fault. Speaking with an attorney first lets you understand your options before anything is on the record.

items.question: What evidence should I keep after a Mission Viejo car accident?
items.answer: Save every photo from the scene, the police or CHP report number, medical records, repair estimates, and any texts or emails from insurers. Write down how you feel each day, since symptoms from a crash often surface later. If the collision happened near a business or intersection with cameras, an attorney can request that footage before it is overwritten.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge me anything to find an attorney?
items.answer: No. Our connection service is completely free, and we are not a law firm. The independent attorney you are matched with works on a contingency basis, so you owe no attorney fee unless your case recovers compensation. You decide whether to hire them after your first conversation.
